newsitem.title: USA: PECO cites Salem, Limerick for lower Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: PECO cites Salem, Limerick for lower Q1 net.

text.p: PECO Energy Co Friday reported lower than expected first quarter earnings, saying the decline from 1996 levels was due primarily to less favorable weather conditions in 1997, accelerated depreciation of assets associated with Limerick Generating Station, and additional fuel costs resulting from the ongoing shutdown of Salem Generating Station.
These decreases were offset partially by the favorable effects of cost containment initiatives.
Earnings per share dropped to $0.49 in the latest quarter from $0.65 in 1996, the utility said.
The First Call consensus estimate for the first quarter was $0.58.
PECO said revenues slipped to $1.16 billion from $1.17 billion in last year's first quarter as power sales increased and natural gas sales declined.

It said total electric sales increased 3.7 percent from the first quarter of 1996. Sales to other utilities increased 15.8 percent compared with last year, while residential and other retail sales decreased 3.9 percent compared with last year.
Natural gas sold and transported decreased 9.4 percent, primarily due to decreased heating sales, which partially offset a corresponding increase in gas transported for others.
